correctness.rationale: On a connected graph, a GH configuration of exact temporal period 3 has all vertices cycle phases or is all resting; a resting vertex cannot neighbor an always-cycling vertex. Fully cycling phase coloring c(v) in Z3 advances iff each vertex has some neighbor c(v)+1. On three connected cubic bipartite incidence graphs with shore sizes m=8/9/10, fix first point phase to zero, enumerate all 3^(m-1) remaining point colors and each allowed line phase; require union of point-successor coverage masks = all point vertices. Factor 3 for global color rotation. The disjoint cover count yields 54036,134478,645180 phase states and 18012,44826,215060 primitive three-orbits. Independent new inclusion-exclusion algorithm using graph encodings reproduced the full three integer counts; no inference from sample or partial census.
residual_risks: Explicit graph encodings are integral to claims; numerics are only period-three census not full transient or other periods. Finite exact exhaustive proof suffices for these three fixed graphs.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: Gravner–Lyu–Sivakoff (2018) defines exactly the 3-color GH dynamics and characterizes synchronization/activity by conservative initial forms and cycle winding (Theorem 3) on arbitrary graphs, but does not list these exact primitive-three phase counts. Published full-subdivision GH 3-periodic formula concerns graphs with inserted degree-2 edge vertices, not these entirely degree-3 Möbius–Kantor/Pappus/Desargues Levi graphs. Other GH line graph and Heawood population counts concern different objects and/or thresholds. A targeted search for named 16/18/20-vertex populations found no numerical implication. Unindexed specialized color-count tables remain a risk.
residual_risks: A hidden existing exact ternary-coloring enumeration on these named incidence graphs could cover the values. Search miss does not prove absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The three historically canonical finite cubic symmetric incidence graphs are natural objects, and exact primitive-three excitation population is a dynamical invariant with a clear definition, useful for benchmarking constrained waves versus total recurrent populations. It is an independently unknown exact census of nontrivial graph/coloring interaction, requiring full 3^(m-1) mask cover enumeration, not a gratuitous tiny arbitrary slice. No general/all-period classification or downstream theorem is required for this independently useful exact finite fact.
residual_risks: Finite exact result should not be advertised as all recurrent populations or as a universal formula for all graphs.
